The Gambling Regulation Act 2024 treats sponsorship, branded merchandise and digital advertising as distinct issues. Its implementation is phased, making the commencement of individual provisions as important as their wording.

The February 2026 commencement order, reproduced in the Law Reform Commission’s July 2026 consolidation, brought parts of the licensing and enforcement framework into operation. However, it expressly excluded Section 159 on sponsorship and several advertising provisions. The Act’s passage therefore cannot be treated as the date every marketing restriction became enforceable.

It was the first time for us to postpone an event, and also the first time we faced sponsorship challenges,” he said. Khubamang added that local promoters were largely staging events to keep the sport alive rather than for commercial gain. “As local promoters, we are just hosting events for the sake of boxing, not for profit-making. “When things were tough, the Ministry of Sport and Arts (MOSA) came on board, which made a huge difference,” he said. However, Khubamang noted that the repeated postponements had also worked in the boxers' favour, giving them more time to train and prepare for their bouts. Despite the setbacks, he said the event eventually went according to plan. During the competition, Kutlwano ‘Chino’ Ogaketse, 28, was crowned the new IBO All Africa Junior Welterweight champion after overpowering South African Aphiwe Mboyiya.

Wider Sports News.title: IPL valuations show why the league’s business model matters more than trophies
Wider Sports News.summary: IPL valuations show why the league’s business model matters more than trophies sports.economictimes.indiatimes.com
Wider Sports News.copy:
Sportico’s 2026 valuations place Mumbai Indians at the top of the IPL at $2.1 billion, but the bigger story is the league’s revenue engine. Central distributions, media rights and strong buyer demand have pushed every franchise above $1.5 billion.

Across the 10-team competition, Sportico pegs combined franchise value at about $17 billion, with an average of $1.7 billion per side. That translates into a league where even the lowest-ranked team is estimated at $1.5 billion, a range that would have seemed improbable when the original eight franchises were sold in 2008. The numbers point to a market that is pricing in not just current earnings, but the durability of the IPL’s centralised commercial engine.

Wider Sports News.title: How franchise sports are reshaping Sri Lanka beyond cricket
Wider Sports News.summary: How franchise sports are reshaping Sri Lanka beyond cricket The Sunday Times, Sri Lanka
Wider Sports News.copy:
The expansion of franchise-based competitions beyond cricket is opening new opportunities for athletes, brands and investors, with the Sri Lanka Padel League helping pioneer a new era for the country’s sporting industry. For decades, cricket dominated Sri Lanka’s sporting landscape, attracting the majority of commercial investment and sponsorship. However, the emergence of franchise-based competitions across multiple sports is beginning to change that picture, creating new opportunities for athletes, businesses and sporting organisations.

Sri Lanka’s franchise-sports journey began with the Sri Lanka Premier League (SLPL) cricket initiative in 2012. Following its failure to establish a sustainable competition, the Lanka Premier League (LPL) was launched in 2020, bringing renewed attention to the commercial potential of the franchise model.

Wider Sports News.title: Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark steps down: On his legacy, the conference’s unique position and what’s next
Wider Sports News.summary: Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark steps down: On his legacy, the conference’s unique position and what’s next The Press Democrat
bullets: Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark will step down and remain in the role through January, having been hired in summer 2022. He announced his exit four years to the day after securing the media rights agreement with Fox and ESPN. His tenure included adding four Pac-12 schools and negotiating an early exit for Texas and Oklahoma. He is presumed to be moving to a role in professional sport.

American Conference commissioner Tim Pernetti is viewed as an obvious candidate to succeed him, while Big 12 board chair Doug Girod of Kansas said the conference does not need a Yormark "twin". The Big 12 is a distant fourth among the conferences by annual revenue distributed to members, making revenue generation an imperative. Yormark signed a Monster Energy sponsorship, partnered with Redbird for access to capital and had spoken of separate football and basketball media deals in the 2030s.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Brett Yormark’s Big 12 epitaph: He came, he saved, he departed. Hired in the summer of 2022, he was the perfect commissioner to guide the conference through the realignment wave, tireless, aggressive, creative — a dealmaker’s dealmaker who locked in the media rights extension, added four schools from the Pac-12 and negotiated an early exit with Texas and Oklahoma.

Notably, Yormark’s announced exit comes four years to the day that he secured the media rights agreement with Fox and ESPN that ensured the Big 12’s survival and helped kneecap the old Pac-12.

Rugby.title: Money-making Nations Championship project carries a cost for fans and players
Rugby.summary: Money-making Nations Championship project carries a cost for fans and players The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
It was a loose kick, tumbling aimlessly end over end into the All Blacks’ half. Their wing Billy Wallace gathered it and sprinted into midfield, through a gap and on into the Welsh half, only their full-back ahead of him now, and with his teammate Bob Deans in the corner of his eye, coming on the inside calling for the ball. Wallace gave the pass and Deans was away, making straight for the posts, tackled at the last moment by Rhys Gabe, and the two of them went sliding for the try‑line together. The ball finished in the tips of Deans’s fingers, at the end of his outstretched arm.

Over the line? On the line? Inches away from the line? No one knows. The referee John Dewar Dallas insisted that Deans never made it. The match finished 3-0 to Wales: the All Blacks’ solitary defeat in 35 games on their 1905 autumn tour of Europe. Lloyd Jones wrote a great novel about that tour, Carl Nixon turned it into a successful play, Nigel Wray paid £180,000 for the jersey the All Blacks captain Dave Gallaher wore on the day. You can still buy a DVD of a “dramatic reconstruction” of the match, and a century later two Kiwi journalists published a book offering what they considered new, definitive proof about what happened.

Rugby.title: Six Nations and Sanzaar agree to sell global broadcast rights together in unique deal
Rugby.summary: Six Nations and Sanzaar agree to sell global broadcast rights together in unique deal The Guardian
bullets: The Six Nations and Sanzaar unions have agreed to sell all their media rights and commercial deals collectively for the first time, under a new revenue-sharing model described as the first of its kind in sport. Southern hemisphere nations will share in profits from the Six Nations and British & Irish Lions tours, while European countries will benefit from deals generated by the Rugby Championship and the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series between New Zealand and South Africa.

A new rights management agency, set up by the 10-person board running the Nations Championship, will manage sales. The new arrangements are expected to affect sponsorship and commercial deals from 2028, but not TV rights until 2030, as existing Six Nations and Sanzaar broadcast rights run to 2029. From 2030 the Six Nations, Rugby Championship and Nations Championship will be sold together, with bespoke packages also available. RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney said the aim is a more efficient approach to the market and higher overall valuations.
Rugby.copy:
The Six Nations and Sanzaar unions have agreed to sell all their media rights and commercial deals collectively for the first time in a new revenue-sharing model. In an innovative arrangement that is the first of its kind in sport, the southern hemisphere nations will receive a share of the profits generated by the Six Nations and British & Irish Lions tours, while the European countries will benefit from broadcast and sponsorship deals generated by the Rugby Championship and the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series between New Zealand and South Africa.

The sales process will be managed by a new rights management agency to be set up by a 10-person board that has been created to run the Nations Championship, which resumes this weekend.

Rugby.summary: Youth Olympic Games: Golden-point winner starts Kenya celebrations in Dakar HSBC SVNS Series
bullets: Kenya won gold in the women's sevens at the Youth Summer Olympics in Dakar, with Mitchelle Chemtai scoring the golden point in extra time to beat tournament favourites Australia in the final at Complexe Iba Mar Diop. The sides were level at 5-5 at the break, and Josephine Kerubo's try and Diana Wanjiku's conversion took the final to a golden point after Australia had edged back ahead through Grace Buchanan. Several members of the Kenya squad first picked up a rugby ball only a year ago.

Madagascar won bronze by beating Czechia 26-10, the first time the nation has won an Olympic medal at any level. In the semi-finals, Australia beat Czechia and Kenya beat Madagascar, after Australia and Madagascar topped their pools. China took fifth place by beating the USA, and Spain beat hosts Senegal for seventh. The women's medallists followed the French, South African and Argentine men's teams onto the podium at Dakar 2026.
Rugby.copy:
Kenya claimed gold in the women’s sevens competition at the Youth Summer Olympics in dramatic fashion, with Mitchelle Chemtai scoring the golden point in extra time to upset tournament favourites Australia in the final at Complexe Iba Mar Diop in Senegal.

The Aussies collected silver with Madagascar winning bronze, the first time the African nation has won an Olympic medal at any level. The silver medallists had been the top seeds to win their first gold since 2014 in the women’s tournament but the Rising Lionesses showed heart, grit and determination in the final to come out with the gold.

Rugby.title: Scrum mechanics and a Gatland cameo: behind the scenes with the Nations Championship’s 13th team
Rugby.summary: Scrum mechanics and a Gatland cameo: behind the scenes with the Nations Championship’s 13th team The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
The 13th team participating at the Nations Championship this month are an intriguing bunch. If you didn’t know much about rugby and had wandered into a first-floor conference room at a hotel near Windsor on Monday you might almost have mistaken them for a gathering of airline pilots from nearby Heathrow. Slim, intelligent, studious … you’d trust them to stay calm on the flight deck.

Stick them in matchday kit, however, and the world’s top rugby union referees do not always enjoy universal respect, certainly online. They can be unflappably brilliant for 79 and a half minutes and yet still be defined by one hairline call barely visible to the naked eye. Every Test in which they are involved is an away game and, popularity wise, they often receive the same unconditional love as traffic wardens and the chancellor of the exchequer.

Rugby.title: 'Berserk' World Rugby law change introduced for autumn as teams left scrambling
Rugby.summary: 'Berserk' World Rugby law change introduced for autumn as teams left scrambling Wales Online
bullets: World Rugby has outlawed hip-drop tackles from 1 November, with players facing at least a penalty and more serious cases risking yellow or red cards, days before the autumn Nations Championship matches begin. The law targets tacklers who grasp an opponent from the side or behind, swing around them and drop their hips or bodyweight onto the ball carrier's legs. World Rugby justified the change on player-welfare grounds, citing research on serious lower-limb injuries.

England vice-captain Ellis Genge called the timing "berserk", questioning why the game still changes rules year to year. Concern about adaptation time grew when referee Christophe Ridley reversed a penalty in Sale Sharks' Premiership match with Harlequins after being told the law was not yet in force. England head coach Steve Borthwick said the team cannot argue against player protection and must be the quickest to adjust.
Rugby.copy:
Ellis Genge has branded rugby's latest law change "berserk" as England's vice-captain questioned the decision to outlaw hip-drop tackles days before the autumn Nations Championship matches begin.

World Rugby has officially outlawed the controversial tackling technique from November 1, with players now facing at least a penalty if they are found guilty of a hip-drop tackle.

Rugby.title: Rugby sevens gold up for grabs in Dakar as eight nations set out on road to Youth Olympic Games glory
Rugby.summary: Rugby sevens gold up for grabs in Dakar as eight nations set out on road to Youth Olympic Games glory HSBC SVNS Series
bullets: Eight nations will contest the women's rugby sevens at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal. Pool matches begin on 2 November and the medal rounds follow a day later. Pool A has Australia, China, Kenya and hosts Senegal, while Pool B has Czechia, Madagascar, Spain and the USA. New Zealand, who won gold in 2018, will not defend their title because the 2022 Games were postponed to 2026 after the pandemic.

This is the fourth summer Youth Olympics and the third to include rugby sevens, which debuted in China in 2014, when Australia won gold. A total of 2,700 athletes will compete across all sports, including 96 in the women's sevens. USA's Luisa Moala, who plays alongside her sister Eseta, will be a flag bearer at the Opening Ceremony on 31 October with volleyball player Caden Phillips.
Rugby.copy:
New Zealand won gold in 2018, with a side featuring current senior sevens stars Risi Pouri-Lane and Mahina Paul. But they will not defend their medal in Dakar, after the scheduled summer Youth Olympics in 2022 were postponed to 2026 in the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic.

While New Zealand are not involved this time around, eight teams will be battling it out for gold medal glory in Senegal over two days of competition. The pool rounds of the women's sevens will start on 2 November and conclude a day later with the medal rounds.

Rugby.title: Family matters as rising rugby sevens stars set their sights high at Youth Olympic Games
Rugby.summary: Family matters as rising rugby sevens stars set their sights high at Youth Olympic Games HSBC SVNS Series
bullets: Canada and Germany will open Pool A of the rugby sevens at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, with hosts Senegal and South Africa completing the group. Reigning champions Argentina, who won gold in Buenos Aires in 2018, are in Pool B with 2014 winners France, Japan and Uganda. The Games scheduled for 2022 were postponed to 2026 after the Covid-19 pandemic.

South Africa are seeking a first sevens gold at the first Olympic event held on African soil. They are coached by former Springbok Sevens player and coach Sandile Ngcobo and include Werner de Bruin and twin brothers Siphesihle and Thubelihle Marule. France's squad of 12 includes sons of former internationals and won the 2026 European Championship in Prague in July. Coach Thomas Darracq said the group aims to deliver a great performance. Argentina's Felipe Ledesma makes his sevens debut.
Rugby.copy:
Pool A rivals Canada and Germany will kick off proceedings, followed by host nation Senegal and South Africa, who complete the group; while reigning Olympic champions Argentina - who claimed gold in Buenos Aires in 2018 - are in Pool B alongside 2014 winners France, who claimed silver four years later, as well as Japan and Uganda.

The scheduled summer Youth Olympics in 2022 were postponed to 2026 in the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic. South Africa, looking to land their first rugby sevens gold in the inaugural Olympic event on African soil, will have high-level experience to count on in the form of South Africa Schools ‘A’ players Werner de Bruin and Siphesihle Marule.

She beat Canada's DaLeaka Menin and England's Megan Jones and Zoe Harrison to the award after a standout year for the Black Ferns. New Zealand flanker Elinor-Plum King, 22, took Breakthrough Player of the Year after scoring three Test tries in her debut international season.

The Black Ferns suffered only one defeat this year under new head coach Whitney Hansen, a 26-19 loss to England in September. Canada lock Sophie de Goede won the award last year, and England full-back Ellie Kildunne won it in 2024. World Rugby chair Brett Robinson praised Olsen-Baker's consistency and influence and King's impact, and said the awards being presented in front of home supporters in Christchurch made the occasion more special.

Australian Darren Cahill, 61, joined the Italian's team in June 2022 when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10 and had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a Grand Slam tournament.

But, together with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi, Cahill has helped Sinner to go on to win five Slams and occupy the world number one spot for 95 weeks. Injury has meant the 25-year-old has not played since winning Wimbledon for the second year in a row in July, which led to Alexander Zverev recently overtaking him at the top of the rankings.

Racket.title: WTA Finals prize money slashed by £4m as 2026 Indian Wells alternates confirmed
Racket.summary: A smaller prize pot after leaving Saudi Arabia. The post WTA Finals prize money slashed by £4m as 2026 Indian Wells alternates confirmed appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: The WTA Finals prize pot has fallen to $10m (£7.42m) for the 2026 edition at Indian Wells, a drop of $5.5m (£4m) from the $15.5m (£11.5m) offered in Riyadh last year. An undefeated singles champion will earn $3.37m (£2.5m) including participation fees, compared with the $5.23m (£3.8m) Elena Rybakina received in 2025. Singles has $8m of the total and doubles $2m, with the winning pair able to earn $725,000 (£538,480).

Each singles player receives $220,000 (£163,379) for taking part and $230,000 (£170,877) for each round-robin win. That rises to $820,000 (£609,214) for a semi-final win and $1.64m (£1.21m) for the title, and an undefeated champion collects 1,500 ranking points. Marta Kostyuk and Diana Shnaider are the alternates, while Iga Swiatek chose not to be one after ending her season with a left thigh injury.
Racket.copy:
The WTA have revealed there will be a significant drop in prize money from last year’s WTA Finals to the 2026 edition in Indian Wells. In 2025, Elena Rybakina went undefeated as she won the title in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, but this year, the season-ending tournament has moved away from the Middle East.

Over the summer, it was announced that Indian Wells would host the season finale, which includes world No 1 Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, French Open champion Mirra Andreeva, and Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, among others.

Racket.title: WTA offers Jodie Burrage support after death threats, online abuse following Chennai defeat
Racket.summary: WTA offers Jodie Burrage support after death threats, online abuse following Chennai defeat Anadolu Ajansı
bullets: The Women's Tennis Association has offered additional support to British player Jodie Burrage after she received death threats and online abuse following her 3-6, 6-3, 7-5 first-round defeat to India's Vaishnavi Adkar at the Chennai Open on Tuesday. The match was Burrage's first WTA Tour singles main-draw appearance in 16 months, and Adkar's first win at WTA level.

WTA staff at the tournament are supporting Burrage alongside its player welfare and Threat Matrix teams. She has been offered a private channel for reporting abusive direct messages and a moderation service that hides offensive public comments. The abuse has been reported to the platforms, and accounts linked to gambling-related abuse could be referred to the Bad Actor programme. The WTA's July report said Threat Matrix secured the removal of 66% of serious abusive posts identified during 2025, and 35 accounts were escalated to law enforcement.

Racket.title: Defeat ends Djokovic's hopes of making ATP Finals
Racket.summary: Novak Djokovic is out of the race to qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin after a second-round defeat by qualifier Rinky Hijikata at the Paris Masters.
bullets: Novak Djokovic, 39, is out of contention for the ATP Finals in Turin after a 2-6 6-3 6-3 second-round defeat by Australian qualifier Rinky Hijikata, ranked 83rd, at the Paris Masters. It is only the second time in 20 seasons that he has failed to qualify when fit. He likely needed a semi-final place in Paris, and said his plan for the next few weeks is "just rest".

Only Americans Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul remain in contention for the final two places, currently held by Frances Tiafoe and Rafael Jodar. Tiafoe lost to Quentin Halys and Alex de Minaur to Tomas Martin Etcheverry. World number one Alexander Zverev and Daniil Medvedev, both already qualified, were also beaten. Djokovic reached the Australian Open final and Wimbledon semi-finals this year but has not reached a Masters 1000 quarter-final.

bullets: For the first time since 1978, four British women and four British men are ranked inside the world's top 100 in the same week, according to the Lawn Tennis Association. Arthur Fery, Cameron Norrie, Jacob Fearnley and Toby Samuel are in the ATP top 100, while Katie Boulter, Sonay Kartal, Harriet Dart and Francesca Jones are in the WTA top 100.

Emma Raducanu sits just outside the WTA top 100 at 106th and has not played since reaching the Queen's Club Championships final in June. Jan Choinski, 30, is the next highest-ranked British man at 113th. Boulter lost to Claire Liu in the Hong Kong Open second round. Fery and Norrie lost in the first round of the Paris Masters to Quentin Halys and Ben Shelton respectively. Samuel plays Slovakia's Luka Pokorny in the first round of the Bratislava Challenger.

Racket.copy:
Hampstead tennis ace Harriet Dart celebrated her crazy week at 2026 Guangzhou Open claiming her first WTA Tour singles title, writes Ziad Chaudry. The 30-year-old defeated Austria’s up-and-coming teenage sensation Lilli Tagger, ranked number 53 on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz world rankings, 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 in two hours and 18 minutes on the hardcourts of Nansha International Tennis Centre, Guangzhou, China to scoop the $37,390 (£27,700) winners’ cheque along with lifting the plate-type trophy.

Dart’s journey to being champion in this WTA250-ranked event began in the first qualifying round beating Hong Kong’s Cheuk Ying Shek 5-7, 7-6(5), 6-1. After easily disposing Mei Yamaguchi from Japan 6-2, 6-1 in the final qualifying round, the GB Billie Jean King Cup regular disposed Russia’s Tatiana Prozorova (6-4, 2-6, 6-2), world-ranked 46 Janice Tjen of Indonesia (6-4, 3-6, 6-3), Spain’s former world number two Paula Badosa (3-6, 6-2, 6-4) and Chinese home favourite Sun Xinran (5-7, 7-6(1), 6-0) before defeating Tagger, the 2025 Roland Garros junior girls singles champion Tagger and this year’s Livesport Prague Open WTA 250 event winner, in the final.

Racket.title: GB's Stojsavljevic, 17, claims first WTA Tour win despite short notice
Racket.summary: British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic beats former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin for her first WTA Tour main-draw win.
bullets: British 17-year-old Mika Stojsavljevic claimed her first WTA Tour main-draw win by beating former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin 6-3 4-6 6-4 at the Hong Kong Open. The world number 411 lost in qualifying but entered the main draw as a lucky loser, and had only an hour's notice that she would be playing. She will face world number 67 Zeynep Sonmez in the second round.

Stojsavljevic became the first Briton in 15 years to win the US Open junior title in 2024 and turned professional in 2025. Earlier this year she beat then world number 56 Talia Gibson in Billie Jean King Cup qualifying in April and reached the quarter-finals of the WTA 125 event in Birmingham. Fellow Briton Katie Boulter's season ended with a 7-5 6-4 loss to American Claire Liu at the same tournament.

Racket.title: P.V. Sindhu qualifies for 2026 BWF World Tour Finals
Racket.summary: P.V. Sindhu qualifies for 2026 BWF World Tour Finals Sportstar
bullets: India's P.V. Sindhu has qualified for the BWF World Tour Finals, the Badminton World Federation confirmed on Wednesday. It is the 31-year-old's sixth appearance at the event and her first since 2021. She qualified in 2022 but withdrew through injury. The tournament takes place in Hangzhou, China, from 9 to 13 December. An Se Young, Akane Yamaguchi, Wang Zhi Yi and Chen Yu Fei have also secured places.

Sindhu won the Hylo Open in Germany last week and is likely to play next at the Syed Modi International in Lucknow, which starts on 24 November. She remains the only Indian to win the women's singles title at the World Tour Finals, having beaten Japan's Nozomi Okuhara in the 2018 final.
Racket.copy:
India’s P.V. Sindhu has qualified for the year-ender BWF World Tour Finals, Badminton World Federation confirmed on Wednesday. This is the 31-year-old’s sixth career appearance in the World Tour Finals and her first since 2021. She had qualified for 2022 but withdrew due to an injury.

The World Tour Finals will take place in Hangzhou, China, from December 9-13. An Se Young, Akane Yamaguchi, Wang Zhi Yi and Chen Yu Fei are the others who have sealed their berths.

Racket.title: 2026 WTA Finals draw: Elena Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, Mirra Andreeva, Coco Gauff, Linda Noskova find out groups
Racket.summary: Which WTA Finals group is tougher? The post 2026 WTA Finals draw: Elena Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, Mirra Andreeva, Coco Gauff, Linda Noskova find out groups appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: The 2026 WTA Finals draw has placed world number one and defending champion Elena Rybakina in Group 1 with No 4 Coco Gauff, No 5 Jessica Pegula and No 8 Linda Noskova. World number two Aryna Sabalenka heads Group 2 alongside No 3 Mirra Andreeva, No 6 Elina Svitolina and No 7 Karolina Muchova. Rybakina is top seed for the first time, and the pair can only meet in the semi-finals or final.

The tournament has moved from Riyadh to the Indian Wells Tennis Garden in California. It starts on Sunday 8 November, with the final on 15 November. Rybakina opens against Noskova, whom she leads 3-0 head-to-head. Noskova, Andreeva and Muchova are making their WTA Finals debuts. Marta Kostyuk and Diana Shnaider are the alternates. Rybakina won last year's title unbeaten, beating Sabalenka in the final.
Racket.copy:
The 2026 WTA Finals draw is out and world No 1 Elena Rybakina appears to have a tough draw in Group 1, whereas Aryna Sabalenka’s group is probably more evenly matched. Defending champion Rybakina is the top seed at the season-ending tournament for the first time following her rise to the top of both the WTA Rankings and Race To Indian Wells.

World No 2 Sabalenka – who has been the top seed the past three years – headlines Group 2 so they can only face each other in either the semi-final or the final. Reigning Australian Open and US Open champion Rybakina has ended up with world No 4 Coco Gauff, No 5 Jessica Pegula and No 8 Linda Noskova in Group A while Sabalenka will face No 3 Mirra Andreeva, No 6 Elina Svitolina and No 7 Karolina Muchova.

Racket.summary: Britain's Jodie Burrage receives death threats and abuse on social media after she is beaten in her first WTA Tour singles match proper for 16 months.
Racket.copy:
Britain's Jodie Burrage received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in her first WTA Tour singles match proper for 16 months. The 27-year-old, ranked 474th in the world, suffered a first-round exit at the Chennai Open after India's Vaishnavi Adkar fought back from a set down to triumph 3-6 6-3 7-5.

Burrage later shared a story on her Instagram account, external with a video scroll of direct messages, including abuse, she was sent following the match. "Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left," said the Londoner in the accompanying message.

Racket.title: Novak Djokovic issues angry complaint to umpire during Paris Masters opener with Valentin Vacherot

Novak Djokovic could not contain his anger during his Paris Masters opener with Valentin Vacherot due to disruption from the crowd. After more than two hours of play, where both players split the first two sets 7-6 (5), 5-7, Djokovic brought up break points on Vacherot‘s serve early in the decider.

Racket.title: Alexander Zverev to become world No. 1 for first time on Monday after Vienna victory, ending long wait fo
Racket.summary: Alexander Zverev to become world No. 1 for first time on Monday after Vienna victory, ending long wait fo The Times of India
bullets: Alexander Zverev will become world No. 1 for the first time when the ATP rankings are published on Monday 2 November. He guaranteed the move by beating the Netherlands' Tallon Griekspoor 6-4 7-5 in the last 16 of the Erste Bank Open in Vienna on Thursday 29 October. The 29-year-old German replaces Jannik Sinner, who ended his season early in October because of right knee inflammation.

Zverev will be the 30th man to hold the top ranking since 1973 and the second German after Boris Becker in 1991. He is the oldest first-time No. 1 since John Newcombe in 1974. He has won the French Open and US Open this season. In 2022 he tore ankle ligaments in his French Open semi-final against Rafael Nadal, which ended his season. Former Austrian No. 1 Thomas Muster joined him in an on-court ceremony in Vienna.
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev has spent years among the leading players in men's tennis, reaching Grand Slam finals and collecting major titles without ever occupying the sport's most coveted ranking position. That wait is finally over after his victory in Vienna, although the milestone carries particular significance for a player whose previous attempt to reach the summit ended with a serious injury and months away from competition.

Zverev secures world No. 1 ranking after beating Griekspoor Alexander Zverev secured the world No. 1 ranking for the first time after defeating Dutch opponent Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 in the last 16 of the Erste Bank Open in Vienna on Thursday, October 29. The victory guaranteed that the 29-year-old German would replace Jannik Sinner at the top when the ATP rankings are published on Monday, November 2, regardless of his subsequent results in the tournament.

Racket.title: Briton Dart reaches first WTA Tour singles final
Racket.summary: A tearful Harriet Dart said it "means the world" to her to qualify for her maiden WTA Tour singles final after battling past to beat China's Sun Xinran at the Guangzhou Open.
bullets: Britain's Harriet Dart has reached her first WTA Tour singles final, beating Chinese wildcard Sun Xinran 5-7 7-6 (6-1) 6-0 in the Guangzhou Open semi-final in just under two and a half hours. The 30-year-old qualifier failed to serve out the first set but saved multiple match points in the second. She then won the decider without losing a game. She will face fourth seed Lilli Tagger or Kaitlin Quevedo in Sunday's final.

Victory would return Dart, the British number five, to the top 100 in the WTA rankings. She has already climbed 14 places to 101st in the live standings. This was only her second tour-level singles semi-final, after the 2024 Transylvania Open, and she made her WTA Tour debut in Eastbourne in 2015. Dart said the result "means the world" after what she called a really long journey.

Racket.title: Jack Draper Opens Up: “I Was Among the Best in the World. Everything Was Taken Away from Me”

bullets: Jack Draper's long injury absence could end in 2027, after persistent bone oedema in his left arm limited him to 15 matches in 2026 and dropped him out of the world's top 150. The 24-year-old reached a Grand Slam semi-final in New York and a career-high ranking of fourth between 2024 and 2025, but played very little after Wimbledon in 2025.

Speaking to Men's Health UK, Draper said he will manage his schedule carefully, with longevity a goal. He criticised the ATP's crowded calendar, saying many decisions have been driven by profit and are putting a generation of players at risk of constant injuries. He also pointed to slower courts and balls and ever fitter athletes, and said he is eager to return with fresh perspective for the second half of his career.
Racket.copy:

However, a seemingly endless succession of injuries slowed his rise. Draper’s breakthrough finally took shape between 2024 and 2025, when he consistently produced his best tennis, reaching a Grand Slam semifinal in New York and climbing to a career-high fourth in the world rankings.

Racket.title: Carolina Marin announces badminton retirement
Racket.summary: Carolina Marin announces badminton retirement SPOTV NOW
bullets: Carolina Marin has announced her retirement from professional badminton at the age of 32. The Spaniard is a three-time world champion and 2016 Olympic gold medallist, and had not competed since suffering a serious knee injury in her semi-final against He Bingjiao at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

She had initially aimed to return at next month's European Championships in Huelva, Spain, but decided against risking further injury. Marin said she would have liked one last appearance on court but did not want to put her body at risk, adding that she effectively retired on court in Paris. Her career included seven European titles, a European Games gold medal and 16 titles on the BWF World Tour and Superseries circuit.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy: Why LIV Golf demise is 'amazing' news
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy: Why LIV Golf demise is 'amazing' news Today's Golfer
Golf.copy:
After making a slice of personal history in Abu Dhabi, Rory McIlroy reflected on the news of LIV Golf’s demise. Not in 21 years and 1,014 rounds on the DP World Tour had Rory McIlroy ever made 11 birdies in a competitive round. But just 24 hours after accepting a two-shot penalty which seemed a significant blow to his hopes of winning a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai, McIlroy conjured another magical personal record as he surged into contention at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

McIlroy’s 9-under par 63 lit up the second round at Yas Links, a blitz that included seven birdies on the back nine. It all came after taking an unplayable and making bogey on the first, as well as the rules incident that threatened to spoil a solid start to his tournament.

Golf.title: Westwood worried for DP World Tour after LIV collapse

bullets: Lee Westwood has said he is worried about the future of the Europe-based DP World Tour following the collapse of LIV Golf. LIV confirmed this week that it intends to wind down after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial support and potential new investors pulled out of a deal to continue it in a new form.

Westwood expects PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp to "play hardball" with the DP World Tour over their strategic alliance, which was extended in July and included annual investment payments of £59m last year. A DP World Tour spokesperson said the tour remains in a "robust and healthy position with strong cash reserves". Westwood noted that only one 2027 prize fund, for the Hero Dubai Desert Classic in January, has been announced so far.

Spain's Jon Rahm, England's Tyrrell Hatton and Italy's Francesco Laporta share the lead at 12 under, while McIlroy sits in a four-strong group alongside Sam Bairstow, Matthew Jordan and Adrian Meronk.

McIlroy had finished the first round two under par, eight shots off the lead, after a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on the 12th hole. He said he had "made peace" with the ruling and played with a clear conscience. He is chasing a fifth consecutive Race to Dubai title and a record-equalling eighth overall, level with Colin Montgomerie. The top 50 in the rankings progress to next week's season-ending DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.

Spain's Jon Rahm, England's Tyrell Hatton and Italy's Francesco Laporta share the lead at 12 under, while McIlroy is part of a four-strong group that includes the English duo of Sam Bairstow and Matthew Jordan, plus Poland's Adrian Meronk.

Golf.title: McIlroy handed two-shot penalty for improving lie
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy is hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie during the opening round of the Abu Dhabi Championship, where Jon Rahm makes a strong start.
bullets: Rory McIlroy received a two-shot penalty for improving his lie during the opening round of the Abu Dhabi Championship at Yas Links, after pressing his club on the grass behind his ball before a chip on the par-four 12th. The penalty turned his six into a quadruple-bogey eight and his four-under 68 into a two-under 70, leaving him eight shots behind leader Francesco Laporta.

The DP World Tour said McIlroy breached rule 8.1b(4), which allows a player to ground the club lightly but not press it on the ground. McIlroy said there was no intent but he was happy to take the penalty, as he did not want people to think he had got away with something. He is tied on two under with Race to Dubai leader Eugenio Chacarra, while Jon Rahm shot a 65 in his first round since leaving LIV Golf.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has been hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie during the opening round of the Abu Dhabi Championship. The six-time major winner was penalised after pressing down on the grass behind his ball with his club before hitting a chip on the par-four 12th at Yas Links.

In a statement, the DP World Tour said McIlroy had breached rule 8.1b(4), which permits a player "to ground their club lightly right in front of or behind the ball". The statement added: "'Ground the club lightly' means allowing the weight of the club to be supported by the grass on or above the ground surface and there is no penalty even if the lie is improved.

As the Northern Irishman then addressed the ball to have another go, his club flattened down some of the rough behind his ball, which was deemed to be improving his lie. That six was then turned into a quadruple-bogey eight as McIlroy's four-under round of 68 became a two-under 70 - in a big blow to his Race To Dubai chances.

Golf.copy:
Race To Dubai leader Eugenio Chacarra struggled to find a fairway during the first round at the Abu Dhabi Championship as he was forced to play with a replacement driver. It wasn't the ideal start for the biggest two weeks of Chacarra's career, as he looks to hold off Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy and become just the third Spaniard to win the Harry Vardon Trophy.

The 26-year-old cracked his regular driver during the Pro-Am in Abu Dhabi and the replacement club wasn't behaving as he missed every fairway on the front nine. Despite the radar being dodgy off the tee, Chacarra still managed to shoot a two-under 70 at Yas Links with no real damage done to his Race To Dubai chances as McIlroy was was given a two-shot penalty to also finish with a 70, while Reed had a nightmare finish in his 74.

Golf.title: LIV to wind down after backers withdraw support
Golf.summary: LIV Golf is set to announce on Thursday it will wind down after a financing firm retracted its support.
bullets: LIV Golf is set to be wound down after BC Partners Credit withdrew support for a proposed new league, LIV 2.0, because it failed to attract enough players. BC Partners had been expected to provide a possible $300m (£223m) in financing after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its backing in April, which led to the league filing for bankruptcy protection in September.

An attorney for LIV is expected to tell a court hearing on Thursday that the LIV 2.0 proposal is not viable. The league had announced a 2027 schedule including an Adelaide event at Kooyonga Golf Club from 18-21 March, but South Australia Premier Peter Malinauskas said he did not expect it to go ahead. The PIF spent more than $5bn (£3.7bn) on the league, and the DP World Tour had said players joining LIV next season would not be tour members in 2027.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf is set to be wound down after its investor withdrew support because the proposed new league failed to attract enough players. LIV had hoped BC Partners Credit would provide a possible $300m (£223m) in financing after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) withdrew its backing in April, leading to the league filing for bankruptcy protection in September.

The funding could have helped the competition move forward in a new form, dubbed LIV 2.0, but BC Partners is understood to have decided it is not viable to pursue a deal. While leading players such as Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia had already walked away, BBC Sport understands that those working on LIV 2.0 had received commitments from co-investors, felt support from within the golf ecosystem and had about 30 players signed up, including major winners.

Golf.summary: Nelly Korda, who has 19 career LPGA wins, took a step closer to the LPGA Hall of Fame on Tuesday without hitting a single shot. The post Nelly Korda arrives on Hall of Fame’s doorstep — without playing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Field lists don’t usually make history, but that’s exactly what happened at 5 p.m. Tuesday when the participants in the LPGA’s penultimate event of 2026, the Annika, were finalized. Absent from the field were Jeeno Thitikul and Miyu Yamashita, the second- and fourth-ranked players in the women’s game, respectively, meaning, after outstanding seasons, they had mathematically eliminated themselves from the LPGA’s Rolex Player of the Year race — and determined a winner.

That would be world No. 2 Nelly Korda, in the wake of her four-win (so far) 2026 and still with three events remaining on the schedule. This is Korda’s second time winning the prize; when she won her first POY, in 2024, she also locked up the title with three events remaining on the schedule.

Golf.title: This rule convinced Rory McIlroy to keep DP World Tour membership
Golf.summary: What made Rory McIlroy want to keep his DP World Tour membership? One rule he wanted to make sure he didn't break. The post This rule convinced Rory McIlroy to keep DP World Tour membership appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Rory McIlroy said at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship on Wednesday that a rule on Ryder Cup captaincy persuaded him to keep his DP World Tour membership. He had considered giving it up in 2019 to focus on the United States, but DP World Tour chief executive Keith Pelley told him that anyone who resigned their membership could not be a Ryder Cup captain or vice captain in future.

McIlroy was speaking for the first time since the latest LIV news, and also discussed golf's 'false economy' era and LIV's push towards an 'arms race'. Sergio Garcia, who recently announced he is leaving LIV to join the DP World Tour next season, has said he wants to be part of the Ryder Cup again. The rule has complicated the path for European captains after Lee Westwood, Ian Poulter, Henrik Stenson and others left for LIV. Stenson was stripped of the 2023 captaincy, and Luke Donald took over.
Golf.copy:
When it comes to pre-tournament press conferences, many can sometimes feel repetitive. Some players simply have more to say than others, or there aren’t as many interesting topics or questions for players to opine on.

But at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship on Wednesday, Rory McIlroy’s time with the media was one many had circled. Speaking for the first time since the latest batch of LIV news dropped, McIlroy, one of the game’s most outspoken and thoughtful figures, riffed on golf’s “false economy” era, LIV’s desire to turn professional golf into an “arms race” and more.

Golf.title: Q&A: DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings bullish on growth amid LIV Golf uncertainty
Golf.summary: Q&A: DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings bullish on growth amid LIV Golf uncertainty Sports Business Journal
Golf.copy:
DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings has “delivered a bullish but, at the same time, realistic update on the circuit,” describing the current uncertainty surrounding LIV Golf as a “chance for all of golf to ‘reset,’” according to a Q&A by Martin Dempster of THE SCOTSMAN. Kinnings spoke openly about several key aspects of the tour, “from speculation about the current health of the circuit to the wellbeing of its members and its plans for membership and invites for next season.” Questions and answers have been edited for clarity and brevity.

Q: What are your thoughts on the DP World Tour in the current landscape? Kinnings: “Our financial structure, like any global business, is complicated. … But the reality shows that there is some real strength, some stuff which makes me bullish about now and what we’re going to do going forward. We have strong cash reserves, but the thing that’s most notable for me is our record sponsorship levels. … We’re over 100 per cent up from 2019 to 2025 with over a billion dollars currently contracted across the Tour. … And it’s not just the sponsorship. You’ve got TV viewership up seven per cent this year alongside consumer levels in terms of ticketing and merch and hospitality up 30 per cent year on year. So people are engaged.”

Golf.summary: Women's TGL: Sky Sports to show exclusive live coverage of new women's team golf league featuring LPGA Tour stars Sky Sports
bullets: Sky Sports has secured exclusive UK and Ireland rights to the WTGL, the new women's team golf league run in partnership with the LPGA Tour. The inaugural season begins on 8 November, and the 2026 and 2027 competitions will both be shown exclusively live, including the play-offs from 20 to 23 December.

The league is played in a custom-built indoor arena in Florida, with five teams of five players who have 48 combined Solheim Cup appearances and 15 major titles between them. Charley Hull, Lottie Woad and Jeeno Thitikul are among the first players. The deal is part of an expansion of Sky's golf rights, which also includes a further two years of TGL presented by SoFi. The men's league grows to seven teams in 2027, and its third season starts on 27 December.
Golf.copy:

Beginning on November 8, the inaugural WTGL season will bring the innovative team golf format - played in a custom-built indoor arena in Florida - to the women's game.

Both the 2026 and 2027 competitions will be broadcast exclusively on Sky Sports as part of an expansion of its golf rights, which also includes a further two years of TGL presented by SoFi.

Golf.summary: Lucas Herbert is one of many pros who have left LIV Golf this fall. He revealed the reason he quit the league as it looks to launch LIV 2.0. The post ‘It’s not enough’: Lucas Herbert reveals his reason for leaving LIV Golf appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Lucas Herbert has said he left LIV Golf to improve his game and give himself better chances in majors, rather than for financial reasons. The Australian joined in 2024 with Cameron Smith's Ripper GC, earned over $25m on course in three seasons and finished tied sixth at the 2026 Open at Royal Birkdale. He told the Tee It Up Podcast that the planned 10 events are not enough to build a season around.

LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September after the Saudi PIF withdrew funding, and BC Partners Global has offered up to $300m for LIV Golf 2.0 if enough players stay. Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Sergio Garcia and Ian Poulter have also left, while Bryson DeChambeau is working to launch LIV 2.0. DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has said LIV 2.0 players will be barred from the tour in 2027.
Golf.copy:
Lucas Herbert knows you probably won’t believe him. Given how things have unfolded in pro golf over the past five years, that’s understandable. But the Australian says he’s leaving LIV Golf for reasons that go beyond his wallet.

“I’m not super caught up in how much money I play for, and I’m sure there’ll be plenty of people who listen to this will think that I’m talking a load of crap,” Herbert told the Tee It Up Podcast. “But genuinely, for me, I wanted to see my game improve, I wanted to give myself the best chance to play well in majors and compete in majors and have opportunities like I had at Birkdale this year.”

On Monday, Compliance Solutions was announced as the presenting sponsor. Compliance is an accounting and tax service provider based in Longwood, Fla., and has an existing relationship with the tour, sponsoring Korn Ferry Tour and PGA Tour Champions events.

“We are proud to have their commitment and support as we prepare to bring this new event online,” said the tour’s executive vice president Dan Glod. The move ends a whirlwind leadup for the tournament. In October 2025, the tour announced it was partnering with Good Good, a popular YouTube influencer brand and apparel company with a sizable following among younger golfers, to host a fall event. This would coincide with Golf Channel reviving the TV show “The Big Break,” which would confer a spot in the Austin field to the winner.

Golf.title: Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship: Five things to know - Articles - Rolex Series

Golf.copy:
The DP World Tour season draws towards a close with its penultimate event as the Rolex Series returns at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. Here are your five things to know. After 40 events spanning five Global Swings, the Back 9, four Majors. three Rolex Series events and 16 national opens, the DP World Tour Play-Offs are upon us. The top 70 available players from the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World tee it up this week at Yas Links before the top 50 then move on to the season-finale at the DP World Tour Championship. Both those events form part of the Rolex Series, with Patrick Reed, Tom Kim and JJ Spaun having already been crowned Rolex Series champions in 2026. Reed's victory at the Hero Dubai Desert Classic helped him to win the International Swing and he is joined by fellow Swing winners Jayden Schaper, Mikael Lindberg, Eugenio Chacarra and Scott Jamieson in the field this week.

With the battle to keep full playing privileges on the DP World Tour having ended with the regular seaon, focus now turns to the quest to be Europe's Number One and lift the Harry Vardon Trophy. Rory McIlroy is looking to equal Colin Montgomerie's record of eight season-long wins with his fifth in a row but the Northern Irishman is in the unusual position of being the hunter rather then the hunted. With three victories this season, it is Chacarra who tops the Rankings ahead of long-time leader Patrick Reed, who has two wins of his own. Then comes Masters champion McIlroy ahead of another two-time 2026 winner in Casey Jarvis, who is the other player who could end this week on top of the Rankings with enhanced points on offer. Those enhanced points mean also mean that the jostling for dual membership with the PGA Tour is far from over, with Joe Dean currently holding the final spot. It truly is All to Play For.

DeChambeau said the teams generated almost $29m in revenue last year against $21m of costs, giving about $8m EBITDA, but player payments were pushed down to them when the original company went bankrupt. The PIF announced it was withdrawing funding after this season, LIV filed for Chapter 11 and BC Partners then stepped in. Under LIV 2.0, players will take an equity share and governance control rather than large upfront salaries, while more than a dozen players, including Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia and Tyrrell Hatton, have announced they are leaving.
Golf.copy:

bullets: Japan's Miyu Yamashita successfully defended her LPGA Maybank Championship title at Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club on Sunday, beating China's Yan Liu by two strokes. A final-round 68, with five birdies and a single bogey at the par-4 ninth, gave the third-round leader a 72-hole total of 22-under.

It was the 25-year-old's fifth career title and her third LPGA Tour win of the season, following the Meijer LPGA Classic and the CPKC Women's Open. Liu, who shot 63 on Saturday and 68 on Sunday, finished on 18-under. Pauline Roussin-Bouchard and Thailand's amateur Marisa Tojai tied for third, with Australia's Robyn Choi fifth on 17-under. The LPGA's Asian swing ends with the Toto Japan Classic at Omitama.
Golf.copy:
Miyu Yamashita successfully defended her title at the LPGA Tour's Maybank Championship on Sunday, beating China's Yan Liu by two strokes. The 2025 Women's Open winner and third-round leader ended with a 72-hole total of 22-under after a final-round 68 on the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club course.

The Japanese golfer sank five birdies with just the one bogey at the par-4 ninth in a near-perfect week where she led from Friday's second round until the final hole. It was the 25-year-old's fifth career title and second in the LPGA Tour this season after she took a wire-to-wire, nine-stroke victory in the CPKC Women's Open at Royal Mayfair in Edmonton, Alberta in August.

bullets: Andrew Novak shot a nine-under 62 in the third round of the Mexico Open at Vidanta Vallarta to build a six-shot lead on 23-under 190. He went five under over the first five holes of the back nine, including an eagle from 279 yards at the par-five 12th, and has made only three bogeys through 54 holes.

Novak, who had a 61 the previous day, is chasing a first individual PGA Tour title; his only win came with Ben Griffin at the Zurich Classic of New Orleans last year. Matthieu Pavon of France is six shots back after a 65, with Doug Ghim a shot further behind after a 64. Pavon's two-year exemption from his 2024 Torrey Pines win expires this year, and he arrived ranked 140th in the FedEx Cup. The final round is live on Sky Sports Golf from 8pm on Sunday.

Golf.title: DP World Tour has major financial reason for stance on LIV Golf stars returning
Golf.summary: DP World Tour has major financial reason for stance on LIV Golf stars returning AOL.com
bullets: The DP World Tour has a financial incentive to welcome back LIV Golf players, with Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia and Tyrrell Hatton having quit LIV to play on the European circuit, where they hold memberships. Its latest filings show it would have made an $85 million loss without a $77 million payment from the PGA Tour under the Strategic Alliance.

It has been mooted that the tour will offer non-members a package of sponsors' invitations, which has divided opinion: Joost Luiten and Eddie Pepperell object, while Rory McIlroy and Justin Rose see a boost. The alliance runs to 2035 but has a break clause next year, and although the tour holds more than $100 million in cash, continued losses could erode it within a few years. Bryson DeChambeau, Cam Smith and Joaquin Niemann are non-members who would strengthen fields.
Golf.copy:
Much as it might displease some of its members, the DP World Tour cannot ignore the financial incentive of welcoming back LIV Golf players seeking a soft landing. With LIV on the brink of collapse, numerous players, including Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia, and Tyrrell Hatton, have quit with the intention of playing on the DP World Tour. They hold memberships on the European circuit and are entitled to return.

Other players are expected to follow, and it has been mooted that DP World Tour bosses will incentivize non-members to quit LIV by offering them a package of sponsors' invitations, a move that has divided opinion among members.

Golf.title: Multiple-Time PGA Tour Winners Involved In Bizarre Rules Incident After Playing Wrong Golf Balls At Mexico Open
Golf.summary: Defending champion Brian Campbell, and four-time PGA Tour winner Tom Kim, got caught up in a costly rules error on Friday, when both played each other's golf balls at the 18th hole
Golf.copy:
The Rules of Golf continue to throw up some weird situations and, at the PGA Tour's VidantaWorld Mexico Open, that's exactly what happened. Tom Kim, who recently received the applause of many for earning gold at the Asian Games, was one of the individuals involved, as was the event's defending champion, Brian Campbell.

Playing the 18th hole, both men found the same greenside bunker at the par 4, with their golf balls coming to rest in the sand. Walking up to the bunker, both splashed out before it was revealed that the pair had played the wrong ball, with Kim playing Campbell's and Campbell playing Kim's.

The key moment came at the par-72 West Course's 7th hole. López Ramírez hit a precise wedge approach that set up a birdie, taking her to 13 under and within two of the lead. Golf.title: Kimsey 'happy to trust tour' over safety in Abu Dhabi
Golf.summary: Golfer Nathan Kimsey says he is "happy to trust" the DP World Tour over player safety during the penultimate event of the 2026 season in Abu Dhabi.
bullets: Nathan Kimsey says he is happy to trust the DP World Tour over player safety at next week's Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, the penultimate event of the season, amid the conflict between Iran, the United States and Israel. He said the tour has contingency plans in place and has kept players informed, and that people he knows in the region say it is safe.

Matt Fitzpatrick voiced concerns about travelling to the Middle East in September and does not appear on the entry list. Kimsey, 72nd in the Race to Dubai, can enter because several players inside the top 70 are not playing; a good week could lift him into the top 50 and a place at the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai. The 33-year-old has earned £448,000 this season with five top-10 finishes.
Golf.copy:
Golfer Nathan Kimsey says that he is "happy to trust" the 2026 DP World Tour regarding player safety during next week's penultimate event of the season in Abu Dhabi. In September, fellow Briton Matt Fitzpatrick had voiced concerns about travelling to the Middle East due to the ongoing conflict between Iran, the United States and Israel.

Fitzpatrick has not been listed, external in next week's entry list for the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, and it remains to be seen if he will play in Dubai the week after for the season finale.
